You are dramatically upgrading the PUBLIC marketing site for Nxeon, a premium cloud VPS host (Next.js 15 App Router + Tailwind v4) at /opt/nxeon. Read /opt/nxeon/CLAUDE.md first. The current landing works but is too basic — the user wants it to "think bigger," excite visitors from the very first section, and add interactivity, effects, and animations. Match/extend the premium dark aesthetic (glassmorphism, navy #060a14, blue→purple gradients #3b82f6→#8a70fb, glow).

STRICT SCOPE — ONLY create/modify:
- /opt/nxeon/app/page.tsx (landing — make it spectacular)
- /opt/nxeon/app/(marketing)/** (existing features/pricing/about/contact + NEW: vps, domains pages)
- /opt/nxeon/components/marketing/** (extend/add)
- /opt/nxeon/app/login/page.tsx, /opt/nxeon/app/register/page.tsx only if needed (keep LoginForm/RegisterForm imports)
Do NOT touch: app/dashboard, app/admin, app/api, lib/, worker/, prisma/, components/ui/, components/portal/, app/globals.css, components/AuthForms.tsx, configs. Do NOT run build/git/systemctl. You MAY run `npx tsc --noEmit`.

EXISTING to reuse: components/marketing/ already has MarketingHeader, MarketingFooter, Logo (NxLogo/NxMark now render /logo.png + /icon.png images), Reveal (IntersectionObserver scroll reveal), sections.tsx (SectionHeading/FeatureCard/TrustBadges/CtaBand), PricingGrid, HeroVisual, DashboardPreview, DeployCatalog, ContactForm, LegalDoc, AuthShell, icons.tsx. CSS classes in globals.css: .card/.glass/.btn-primary/.btn-secondary/.btn-ghost/.grad-text/.page-title/.section-label, colors navy-950..600/brand-300..600/accent-blue/accent-cyan, animations animate-fade-up/animate-pulse-dot. Live data via `import { db } from "@/lib/db"` (read-only): `db.plan.findMany({where:{active:true},orderBy:{sortOrder:"asc"}})` (now 4 plans), `db.osTemplate.findMany({where:{active:true}})` (5 OS + 7 control panels + 6 apps, has category/family/version/logo fields). `export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"`.

REQUIREMENTS:

1. **Bigger logo** — the logo currently renders too small. In MarketingHeader make the logo ~40-44px tall (it's /logo.png, a wide lockup). Ensure it's crisp and prominent.

2. **Spectacular hero (excite from the first section)** — rebuild the hero to be bold and alive: large animated gradient headline, an animated background (CSS — e.g. moving aurora/gradient mesh, subtle animated grid, or floating glow orbs; pure CSS keyframes via a client component with a scoped <style> tag since globals.css is off-limits), micro-interactions, and motion. Add at least: an animated element that conveys "instant deploy" (e.g. a looping typewriter/terminal that "types" `nxeon deploy --plan pro --os ubuntu` then shows a success line, or an animated deploy-progress card). Keep it performant and tasteful (no seizure-inducing flashing). Client components ("use client") for anything interactive/animated.

3. **Home-page domain checker** — a prominent interactive section (client component) where visitors type a domain and see live availability + price. Call the EXISTING endpoint `GET /api/domains/check?q=<query>` (returns `{configured, results:[{domain, available, premium, priceCents, renewCents}]}`; if `configured:false` show a tasteful "domains launching soon" state but keep the input usable). Debounce input (~400ms), animate results in, show available domains with price + a "Register" button linking to /register (or /dashboard/domains/register?domain=X). Make it feel delightful.

4. **Interactive/animated elements throughout** — hover-lift on cards, animated stat counters (count up on scroll-in via IntersectionObserver), gradient borders, glow on hover, smooth Reveal staggering, an animated "deploy anything" catalog (the 18 images) with tab switching, a world/network motif for global reach (CSS/SVG, no external assets). Add tasteful motion to pricing and feature sections.

5. **Per-plan recommendation/tip (generated from specs)** — add a helper (e.g. in components/marketing/planTips.ts) `planTip(plan)` that returns a short "great for…" line derived from cpuCores/ramMB/diskGB. Suggested logic: ramMB<=2048 → "Personal sites, dev/staging, bots, VPNs"; ramMB<=4096 → "WordPress & WooCommerce, small game servers, CI runners"; ramMB<=8192 → "Busy sites, databases, Docker stacks, small multiplayer servers"; else → "High-traffic apps, big databases, multiple sites, heavy workloads". Show this tip on each pricing card (landing + /pricing + /vps). Make it feel like smart guidance.

6. **New "VPS" services page** at app/(marketing)/vps/page.tsx — a dedicated product page for VPS hosting: hero, what's included (root access, NVMe, snapshots, backups, firewall, console, one-click apps), the deploy catalog, full pricing with tips + comparison, use-cases, FAQ, CTA. Link it from the header nav.

7. **New "Domains" page** at app/(marketing)/domains/page.tsx — a product page for domain registration: hero with the domain checker (reuse the component), popular TLDs + pricing (you can show a curated TLD price list — pull from the checker or a small static list clearly noted, since live pricing needs a query), features (free WhoisGuard, DNS management, one-click point-at-VPS), FAQ, CTA. Link from header nav.

8. **Header nav** — restructure to include: VPS, Domains, Pricing, Features (+ About/Contact can move to footer or a menu), Login, Get Started. Consider a "Products" grouping. Mobile hamburger must work. No dead links — only link to pages that exist (your pages + /login /register /dashboard/*).

Quality bar: this should look like a billion-dollar cloud company's site — modern, animated, exciting, cohesive with the dark premium portals, fully responsive (mobile-first, hamburger nav, no horizontal scroll). Real data only (plans/images from Prisma; domain checker from the real API). All animations CSS/JS with no external libraries or assets. tsc --noEmit must pass. Report: files created/changed, the animation techniques used, and confirm tsc clean.

1	# Nxeon — VPS hosting platform
2	
3	Hostinger-style VPS hosting platform running on this Proxmox VE 9 dedicated server (OVH KS-GAME, i7-7700K, 64GB RAM, 2×450GB NVMe ZFS mirror + 4TB HDD backup pool).
4	
5	## Architecture
6	
7	- **Web panel**: Next.js 15 (App Router, server actions) + Tailwind v4, served by `nxeon-web.service` on port 3000, behind nginx on port 80. Public IP: 51.79.162.96.
8	- **Worker**: `worker/index.ts` run by `nxeon-worker.service` (as root — it manages iptables). Polls the `Job` table every 3s and executes provisioning/lifecycle jobs against the Proxmox API.
9	- **DB**: PostgreSQL 17, database `nxeon`, Prisma ORM ([prisma/schema.prisma](prisma/schema.prisma)). Use `npm run db:push` after schema changes.
10	- **Proxmox**: API token auth (`nxeon@pve!platform`, creds in `.env`). Templates: VMID 9000 (Ubuntu 24.04), 9001 (Debian 13), cloud-init based, cloned onto ZFS storage `vmdata`.
11	- **Networking**: VMs attach to NAT bridge `vmbr1` (10.20.0.0/24, gateway .1). IPs allocated from 10.20.0.100–250 ([lib/ipam.ts](lib/ipam.ts)). SSH exposed via DNAT port forwards 20000–29999 in iptables chain `NXEON_FWD`, rebuilt from DB by [worker/network.ts](worker/network.ts) — never edit that chain by hand.
12	- **Cloud-init**: vendor snippet at `/tank/backup/snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml` (installs qemu-guest-agent, enables root password SSH).
13	
14	## Portals & design system
15	
16	- Customer portal (`app/dashboard/**`) and admin ops portal (`app/admin/**`) are separate sidebar apps sharing `components/portal/Shell.tsx` (sidebar, topbar, notifications bell, ⌘K command palette backed by `/api/search`).
17	- Design system lives in `app/globals.css` (glass cards, gradient buttons, navy palette) + `components/ui/primitives.tsx` + `components/ui/charts.tsx` (dependency-free SVG charts). Use these — do not add chart libraries.
18	- Admin impersonation: `impersonateUser()` sets a signed cookie; `currentUser()` returns the target, `realUser()` the actual admin; banner + exit handled in Shell. Admin pages call `realUser`/`requireAdmin` and refuse to render while impersonating.
19	- Metrics come from Proxmox RRD via `/api/metrics` (node for admins, per-server for owners).
20	
21	## Integrations (activate via /opt/nxeon/.env)
22	
23	- **Stripe**: `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` + `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` → wallet top-ups switch from demo gateway to Checkout (`/api/stripe/checkout`, webhook `/api/stripe/webhook`, event `checkout.session.completed`, idempotent by session id).
24	- **Namecheap** (`lib/namecheap.ts`): `NAMECHEAP_API_USER/KEY/USERNAME/CLIENT_IP` (+`NAMECHEAP_SANDBOX=1` for testing) → domain search/register/renew/DNS management. TLD retail prices in `TLD_PRICES`.
25	- **GitHub**: remote `origin` = `git@github.com:santino1233/nxeon.git` via deploy key `/root/.ssh/nxeon_deploy`. Every commit auto-pushes via `.git/hooks/post-commit`. `.env`/credentials are gitignored — never commit secrets.
26	
27	## Conventions
28	
29	- All state changes to VMs go through `Job` rows — the web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly (read-only status calls are OK).
30	- One in-flight job per server (enforced in `serverAction`).
31	- Admin-only actions live in [lib/actions.ts](lib/actions.ts) and must call `requireAdmin()`.
32	- Free VPSes: `Server.isFree = true`, no billing, `expiresAt = null`.
33	- Wallet amounts are integer cents.
34	
35	## Commands
36	
37	- Build: `npm run build` (must pass before restarting services)
38	- Deploy after changes: `npm run build && systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker`
39	- Worker logs: `journalctl -u nxeon-worker -f`
40	- E2E test: `npx tsx scripts/e2e-test.ts` (orders a real VM; delete it afterwards via a DELETE job)
41	- Admin credentials: `/root/nxeon-credentials.txt`
42	
43	## Domains & TLS
44	
45	- **Single source of truth**: `/etc/nxeon/domains.env` (BASE_DOMAIN, ADMIN_HOST, STAGING_HOST, CERTBOT_EMAIL). The domain is a placeholder (`revsports.ca`) until the real one is bought. **Never hardcode the domain anywhere in app code** — the app uses `APP_URL` / `NXEON_ADMIN_HOST` from `.env`, and nginx vhosts are generated.
46	- **To migrate to a new domain**: edit `/etc/nxeon/domains.env`, point DNS (A records for apex, www, admin host, staging host) at the server, then run `scripts/configure-domains.sh`. It regenerates nginx vhosts, obtains Let's Encrypt certs, updates APP_URL in both `.env`s, and restarts web. That's the whole migration.
47	- **Routing**: customer portal on `https://BASE_DOMAIN` (admin path returns 404 here — hidden); admin ops portal on `https://ADMIN_HOST` (secret subdomain, root 302→/admin); staging on `https://STAGING_HOST`. HTTP→HTTPS 301. Real LE cert (auto-renews via certbot timer); self-signed fallback for bare-IP.
48	- Secure cookies are on (`COOKIE_SECURE=1`) now that real HTTPS exists. Stripe webhook is live at `https://BASE_DOMAIN/api/stripe/webhook`.
49	
50	## Environments
51	
52	- **Production**: `/opt/nxeon`, DB `nxeon`, services `nxeon-web` (port 3000) + `nxeon-worker`, nginx port 80, VPS pools IP 10.20.0.100–250 / SSH ports 20000–29999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD`. Public: http://51.79.162.96
53	- **Staging**: `/opt/nxeon-staging`, DB `nxeon_staging`, services `nxeon-staging-web` (port 3001) + `nxeon-staging-worker`, nginx port 8080, ISOLATED VPS pools IP 10.20.0.50–99 / SSH ports 30000–30999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD_STG`, VM tag `nxeon-staging`. Public: http://51.79.162.96:8080. Admin creds: `/root/nxeon-staging-credentials.txt`.
54	- Instance differences are driven entirely by `.env` (NXEON_ENV, NXEON_COOKIE_NAME, NXEON_NAT_CHAIN, NXEON_TAG, NXEON_IP_START/END, NXEON_SSH_PORT_START/END, NXEON_CRED_FILE, PORT, APP_URL) — the code is identical.
55	- **Deploy flow**: push to GitHub → `scripts/deploy-staging.sh [ref]` builds+migrates+restarts staging → verify at :8080 → `scripts/promote-production.sh` rebuilds+restarts production. The improvement agent should test changes on staging before promoting.
56	
57	## Safety rules
58	
59	- NEVER touch VMIDs 9000–9999 (templates) except to add new templates.
60	- Staging and production share the Proxmox node but never overlap: staging only ever allocates IPs .50–.99 and ports 30000–30999. Never point staging pools at production ranges.
61	- Test risky/provisioning changes on staging (`scripts/deploy-staging.sh`) before promoting to production.
62	- Never `qm destroy` a VM that has a `Server` row — always go through a DELETE job.
63	- Do not commit `.env`. Do not print the Proxmox token into logs or docs.
64	- Always `git commit` working states; never leave the tree broken — services restart from this directory.

I see the core issue now: the `/api/domains/check` endpoint requires authentication, but the public marketing site won't have authenticated users. Since I can't modify the API, my client component needs to gracefully handle the 401 response by treating it the same way as an unconfigured domain checker.

I'll build the component to attempt the fetch, but when it hits a 401, I'll show a friendly state that prompts users to sign in or indicates the feature is launching soon, while keeping the input usable and displaying a curated static list of TLD prices from the registrar library. This way the interface degrades gracefully within the constraints.
